To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relationship between competition and innovation is not linear, that it is U-shaped, that the inverted-U shape is robust to different specifications of the model and that it is robust to different measures of competition, innovation and product quality.
the relationship between competition and innovation is nonmonotonic.
the degree of market concentration affects the level of innovation in product quality in the same way that it affects the level of investment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How does product quality affect firm and industry performance?
the impact of competition on innovation in product quality in the context of transition economies.
the relationship between competition and innovation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
competition is a two-edged sword.
the degree of competition is an important factor in the innovation process.
there are some positive effects of competition on innovation in product quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
competition and product quality are positively related, and this relationship is stronger in countries with higher levels of competition.
competition matters for innovation, but the relationship between them is complex and depends on the degree of competition.
we have shown that the number of firms matters in a market, and that this number is not only a measure of competition, but also a measure of the potential to innovate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a moderate degree of competition is beneficial for innovation in quality.
the degree of competition in an industry matters for the incentives for firms to innovate.
the relationship between the degree of market competition and product quality innovation is more complicated than the standard view of a positive effect.
